verbalization: Succinic acid interacts with Slc13a1 and Slc13a2, which are part of the sodium-coupled sulfate, di- and tri-carboxylate transporters. These transporters are involved in the transport of carboxylic acids, including succinic acid, across cellular membranes. The evidence suggests that succinic acid binds to these transporters, potentially influencing their function. Slc13a3, which is part of the same pathway, is likely a downstream target of these transporters. The integration of the evidence implies that succinic acid may regulate Slc13a3 through its interaction with the sodium-coupled sulfate transporters, possibly by modulating transporter activity or by affecting the cellular environment in which these transporters operate. This mechanism highlights a potential role for succinic acid in the regulation of transporters involved in carboxylic acid transport, with Slc13a3 being a key target in this process.
